_readme: THE FILL IS HELD HERE. mapsee_ingest_osm_amenities.py --frontier reads this file: an area named below examines only its first F candidates, so every visit still re-reads (and, through the sync's --skip-unchanged, refreshes) what is already stored and adds only what OSM gains inside that window. Keys starting with '_' are notes and are skipped.

WHY. The first full turn of all 260 hubs ended 2026-10-25 and inserted 465,774 rows in five Sundays, 86% of them pin_only furniture, into a Supabase Micro instance. These 94 hubs still held 415,471 unexamined candidates past F (791,471 in all; Tokyo 21,134, Yokohama 17,998, Dusseldorf 17,114, Essen 16,891, Amsterdam 16,350 the deepest), which the cursor would have turned into roughly 0.24-0.34M more rows over about 30 weeks.

WHICH HUBS. F is each hub's cursor on 2026-10-27, and a hub is here only if its cursor has ONLY EVER ADVANCED: every one of these 94 appears exactly once in `git log -p osm_amenity_cursor.json`, as a new key at 4000, in one of the five weekly commits d7ab8b2 (09-27), 5578991 (10-04), d0cda9b (10-11), 7d9cad4 (10-18), 6c3203c (10-25). A hub whose walk has ever come back round has stored rows past any F, and a frontier would freeze them; `_left_out` names those and the proof.

NOT HERE ON PURPOSE: the 154 hubs at cursor 0 (read whole on every visit, at most 4,000 candidates); Albuquerque, Providence and Bremen (no cursor yet, so their first visit reads up to 4,000 as before).

WHAT IT DOES NOT FREEZE AND WHAT IT DOES. A --kinds run ignores this file (a frontier is a position in the FULL list), which is also how the four buildings past F are refreshed: the 2026-09-22 dispatches 35699268602 and 35699326816 wrote every hub's community centres, libraries, markets and dog parks with --kinds --ignore-cursor, an estimated 46,367 of them past these frontiers, and only another such dispatch reaches them while the hold stands.

LIFTING IT is one repository variable: OSM_AMENITY_FILL=on (or the `fill` dispatch input for one run), or deleting this file. A held visit leaves the cursor at 0 (the walk wraps inside F), so the first visit after a lift re-reads [0, F) once before the fill moves on.

_left_out.Washington DC: its cursor went 0 -> 4000, and the 0 was a WHOLE READ: dispatches 35692053574 and 35697114519 (2026-09-22, --max-places 12000 and 13000) examined all 11,324 and then all 12,583 candidates, so everything past 4000 is stored
_left_out.Grenoble: its cursor says 4000, but the 2026-10-25 Reno job's substring --only pulled Grenoble's window from 4000 (job 121138829093: 'Grenoble: 5667 candidate(s) ... from 4000 examined'), so it has been read whole without the cursor file knowing
